_readme: Canonical answers for the screening questions that appear on LinkedIn Apply, Greenhouse, Workday, Lever and similar ATS forms. Used by /apply-job and /auto-apply; low-confidence or novel questions fall back to deep_experience.json and a human-review gate.
Copy to data/application_profile.json, replace every Alex Example value with your own, then run: chmod 600 data/application_profile.json

REQUIRED fields: identity.first_name, identity.last_name, identity.email and identity.phone must be present; the pipeline scripts raise an error if any of them is missing. Everything else is optional with sensible defaults.
This file contains contact details and home address. It must NEVER be committed to git (it is covered by .gitignore) and should stay chmod 600.

The verified_form_answers block at the bottom is the authoritative lookup table for exact ATS field labels seen in real forms. It compounds over time: whenever the walker encounters and correctly answers a new label, add it here so future runs answer it deterministically instead of re-deriving it.

identity._pronouns_comment: Optional; leave empty to skip pronoun fields on forms.
identity.address_note: Home address for ATS forms only. It must NOT appear on any CV or public document.

by_country._comment: One entry per country you apply in. The walker answers right-to-work and sponsorship questions from this block; countries not listed are escalated to a human.

Canada.notes: Canadian citizen, full right to work in Canada.

United States.notes: No US work authorisation. Requires TN / H-1B or equivalent sponsorship. Open to sponsorship.

United Kingdom.notes: Requires a UK Skilled Worker visa. Open to sponsorship.

availability.work_mode_notes: Prefers hybrid in Toronto or remote within Canada.

compensation._policy: Salary expectations vary by role and should be researched per application. 'floor' values are the acceptance threshold (offers below are rejected); do NOT anchor form answers to them. If the JD states a range, answer within it; if not, derive an expectation from role title, seniority and employer type before falling back to the default target.
compensation._default_target_comment: default_target (number) and currency_symbol (string) are the currency-neutral keys the scripts read. The legacy per-currency key default_target_gbp is still accepted for backwards compatibility.
compensation._stretch_use: Use the stretch value when the JD signals senior level or states an upper band above the default target.
compensation.bonus_expectation_notes: Open to discuss; happy for total compensation to include bonus and equity.

candidate_summary_for_salary_research._use: Concise anchor passed to salary research so band lookups are grounded in actual experience. Update when your employment situation or title changes.
candidate_summary_for_salary_research.current_status: Employed as Business Analyst at ExampleCorp, Toronto.
candidate_summary_for_salary_research.headline: 3 years at ExampleCorp as Business Analyst (2023 - present). Strong SQL, Python, reporting automation and stakeholder management; no people-management experience.
candidate_summary_for_salary_research.right_to_work: Canadian citizen; sponsorship needed for the US and UK.
candidate_summary_for_salary_research.salary_anchor_signal: 3 years total experience. Strong fit for Business Analyst / Operations Analyst / Data Analyst at non-senior level; stretch into senior analyst or bizops manager titles.

Spanish.notes: Comfortable in casual conversation; not a working language.

experience_years._comment: Used to answer 'how many years of experience with X' questions deterministically. Overall figure first, then per-skill overrides; skills not listed fall back to an LLM judgement with a review gate.
experience_years.notes: 3 years overall at ExampleCorp (2023 - present). Skills below 2 years reflect side projects (budget tracker, league stats dashboard) rather than day-job usage.

demographic_optional._comment: All demographic questions are optional on ATS forms. The safe default is 'Prefer not to say' for every field; change individual values only if you actively want to disclose. The scripts read these demographic fields (ethnicity, disability_status, veteran_status, etc.) from this block for diversity questions, defaulting each to 'Prefer not to say' when a key is absent.

misc_common_questions.why_this_company: See cover letter; tailored per role.
misc_common_questions.willing_to_sign_non_compete: Depends on scope; willing to discuss.

strengths_signal_questions._comment: Short first-person answers to common open questions, written once and reused. Keep them honest and specific to your own record.
strengths_signal_questions.biggest_strength: Turning vague operational questions into structured analysis that people act on; for example the onboarding process redesign at ExampleCorp that cut turnaround time by 30%.
strengths_signal_questions.biggest_weakness: I can spend too long polishing analysis before sharing it. I now share a rough draft early and iterate with stakeholders instead.
strengths_signal_questions.why_leaving_current_role: I have learned a lot at ExampleCorp, but I am looking for a role with more scope for advanced analytics and a bigger data platform to work with.
strengths_signal_questions.five_year_goal: Leading an analytics or business operations function, combining hands-on analysis with team responsibility.

question_matching_hints._comment: Regex/substring hints the screening answerer uses to route a raw form question to the right section of this file.

verified_form_answers._description: Exact ATS form labels observed in real submissions, mapped to the answer to fill. Matched by label substring (case-insensitive) before falling back to regex-based answering. 'kind' tells the walker how to fill: 'fill_text' for textboxes, 'select' for comboboxes, 'click_option' for typeahead listboxes, 'check' for required checkboxes, 'compute_salary_per_role' for per-role salary research. Add new labels as the walker encounters them so this table compounds over runs.

How many years of relevant experience do.note: Defaults to overall_professional; prefer the by_skill lookup for skill-specific questions.

How many years of work experience do you.note: From experience_years.by_skill. Example of a skill-specific years question.

What are your salary expectations for th.note: Never a fixed number: research per role. Most ATS validation requires a single decimal number, not a range string.
